Item 1. Business

Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis across Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

The Company's business, reputation, results of operations, and financial condition can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including those described below. When any one or more of these risks materialize, the Company's business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition, and stock price can be materially and adversely affected.

Global economic conditions and geopolitical tensions could adversely impact our business, revenue, and margins. Volatility in macroeconomic conditions, including fluctuations in interest rates, inflation, consumer confidence, currency exchange rates, and credit markets, affects purchasing decisions by consumers and businesses for the Company's premium hardware and digital services.

Our operations rely on complex global semiconductor supply chains subject to disruption. Component suppliers and outsourced manufacturing partners are concentrated in East Asia. Disruptions resulting from natural disasters, geopolitical instability, regional conflicts, trade disputes, tariffs, or pandemics could impair product assembly schedules and inflate logistics expenses. Furthermore, intense competition across consumer electronics and platform ecosystems requires continuous, massive capital allocation toward research and development.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes contained in Item 8 of this report.

Total net sales grew 2% year-over-year driven by Services revenue acceleration. Net sales were $391.0 billion in fiscal 2024 compared to $383.3 billion in fiscal 2023. Services revenue reached an all-time record, propelled by double-digit growth in advertising, cloud services, and payment services. Gross margin was $180.7 billion, representing a gross margin percentage of 46.2%, an increase of 210 basis points compared to the prior fiscal year.

Operating margin was 30.7%, reflecting disciplined operational management and operating expense leverage. Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $118.2 billion, enabling $95.0 billion in share repurchases and $15.2 billion in cash dividends paid to common shareholders. We believe our existing cash balances, commercial paper facilities, and sustained operating cash flows will remain sufficient to satisfy our capital requirements, contractual obligations, and capital return programs for the foreseeable future.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

The Company is exposed to market risk from changes in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.

Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

Consolidated statements of operations follow. Total assets as of September 28, 2024 were $364.98 billion, compared to $352.58 billion in 2023. Total liabilities were $308.03 billion, and total shareholders' equity was $56.95 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $156.65 billion across all maturities.
